claims: The 25th Amendment was ratified in 1967 following the JFK assassination.
Under Section 1 of the 25th Amendment, if the President is removed, dies, or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.
Under Section 2 of the 25th Amendment, the President nominates a new Vice President, confirmed by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress.
Under Section 3 of the 25th Amendment, the President declares in writing an inability to serve, making the Vice President Acting President until a written declaration to the contrary is submitted.
Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet can declare the President incapacitated, immediately making the VP Acting President.
Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, if the President disputes this, Congress decides the issue.
In 1973, Gerald Ford was nominated as Vice President by Richard Nixon after Spiro Agnew resigned.
In 1974, Gerald Ford became President following Richard Nixon's resignation.
In 1974, Nelson Rockefeller was appointed Vice President by Ford.
Presidents Reagan (1985), G.W. Bush (2002, 2007), and Biden (2021) used the 25th Amendment for temporary transfers during medical procedures requiring anesthesia.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been used.
